biological.citation: TMEM63 proteins function as monomeric high-threshold mechanosensitive ion channels (PMID: 37543036)
biological.summary: TMEM63B functions as a monomeric mechanosensitive ion channel with small conductance and high activation thresholds. Structural analysis revealed a single highly restricted pore and conformational differences in the mechano-sensing domain IL2 and gating helix TM6 compared to dimeric OSCA channels, demonstrating that oligomerization state affects mechanosensitivity.

biological.citation: Mechanosensitive channels TMEM63A and TMEM63B mediate lung inflation-induced surfactant secretion (PMID: 38127458)
biological.summary: TMEM63B loss-of-function in mice results in atelectasis and respiratory failure due to deficient surfactant secretion. TMEM63B localizes to the limiting membrane of lamellar bodies in alveolar type 2 cells and activation during cell stretch facilitates surfactant and ATP release, triggering Ca2+ signaling and exocytic fusion of additional lamellar bodies.

biological.citation: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration (PMID: 37421948)
biological.summary: Heterozygous TMEM63B variants (p.Val44Met, p.Arg433His, p.Thr481Asn, p.Gly580Ser, p.Arg660Thr, p.Phe697Leu) modeled in Neuro2a cells demonstrate inward leak cation currents in isotonic conditions and impaired response to hypo-osmotic challenge with reduced Ca2+ transients. Ectopic expression of p.Val44Met and p.Gly580Cys variants in Drosophila resulted in early death.

biological.citation: Structural and functional basis of mechanosensitive TMEM63 channelopathies (PMID: 40480214)
biological.summary: TMEM63B p.V44M is a gain-of-function mutation that evokes constitutive lipid scramblase activity without enhancing channel activity. Cryo-EM structures reveal major rearrangements of pore-lining helices creating a lateral cleft, with disruption of a surface-proximal hydrophobic latch (putative force-sensing module) triggering lipid scrambling through the cleft.

biological.citation: Phospholipid scrambling induced by an ion channel/metabolite transporter complex (PMID: 39217145)
biological.summary: TMEM63B forms a heterodimer with the thiamine transporter SLC19A2 that induces phospholipid scrambling upon Ca2+ stimulation. CRISPR screening identified TMEM63B as a PLS-inducing factor, with disease-related TMEM63B mutants inducing constitutive PLS. The complex functions with Ca2+-activated K+ channel KCNN4 to regulate PLS activity.

biological.citation: Expression and localization of the mechanosensitive/osmosensitive ion channel TMEM63B in the mouse urinary tract (PMID: 38724885)
biological.summary: TMEM63B is expressed in proximal tubule epithelial cells, intercalated cells of the collecting duct, and thick ascending limb epithelium in kidneys. In the urinary tract, TMEM63B is expressed in urothelium lining the renal pelvis, ureters, bladder, and urethra, as well as in seminal vesicles, vas deferens, prostate, and vaginal epithelium.

biological.citation: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scrambling by TMEM63B to control plasma membrane lipid distribution (PMID: 39424995)
biological.summary: TMEM63B functions as a membrane structure-responsive lipid scramblase localized at the plasma membrane and lysosomes, activating bidirectional lipid translocation upon changes in membrane curvature and thickness. The V44M mutation confers constitutive scramblase activity, disrupting phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin asymmetry in the plasma membrane.

biological.citation: TMEM63 mechanosensitive ion channels: Activation mechanisms, biological functions and human genetic disorders (PMID: 37857161)
biological.summary: TMEM63B is a mechanosensitive and osmosensitive ion channel with heterozygous variants associated with intellectual disability, abnormal motor function, and brain morphology abnormalities. TMEM63 proteins are ubiquitously expressed and function in detecting mechanical and osmotic stimuli across diverse tissues.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Identifying causal genes modulated by rare regulatory variants in Alzheimer's disease (T. Patel)
biological.summary: Rare non-coding variants in gene regulatory elements interacting with TMEM63B were identified in a VEGFA-TMEM63B locus cluster significantly associated with Alzheimer's disease risk in microglial cells, suggesting TMEM63B expression may be modulated by rare regulatory variants in disease-relevant cell types.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - Human and mouse essentiality screens as a resource for disease gene discovery (P. Cacheiro et al.)
biological.summary: TMEM63B was identified through integration of mouse knockout viability data and human cell line essentiality screens as a novel gene associated with intellectual disability. IMPC mouse models of TMEM63B show neurological and movement phenotypes partially modeling human disease.
